Construct the PAG of a MAG's Markov equivalence class

Source: R/operations.R
mag_to_pag.Rd

Returns the Partial Ancestral Graph of the Markov equivalence class of a maximal ancestral graph. It has the same skeleton as cg, since Markov equivalent MAGs share their adjacencies, and each endpoint carries an arrowhead or a tail when every member of the class has that mark there, and a circle otherwise.

Usage

mag_to_pag(cg)

Arguments

cg

A caugi object of class "AG" that is maximal.

Value

A caugi object of class "PAG".

Details

Starts from the skeleton with every mark a circle, orients the unshielded colliders of cg, and closes under Zhang's complete orientation rules R1-R10. No separating sets are needed: Markov equivalent MAGs share their unshielded colliders, and R4 reads collider status off cg.

References

Zhang, J. (2008). On the completeness of orientation rules for causal discovery in the presence of latent confounders and selection bias. Artificial Intelligence, 172(16-17), 1873-1896.

See also

Other operations: condition_marginalize(), count_dags(), dag_from_pdag(), dag_to_pag(), enumerate_dags(), exogenize(), latent_project(), meek_closure(), moralize(), mutate_caugi(), normalize_latent_structure(), pag_to_mag(), skeleton()

Examples

mag <- caugi(A %-->% B, C %-->% B, class = "AG")
mag_to_pag(mag) # A o-> B <-o C: both arrowheads are invariant
#> <caugi object; 3 nodes, 2 edges; simple: TRUE; session=0x5b8a91e88720>
#>   graph_class: PAG
#>   nodes: A, C, B
#>   edges: Ao->B, Co->B

# A chain has no invariant marks: it is equivalent to the reversed chain
# and to the fork.
mag_to_pag(caugi(A %-->% B, B %-->% C, class = "AG"))
#> <caugi object; 3 nodes, 2 edges; simple: TRUE; session=0x5b8a9215a7b0>
#>   graph_class: PAG
#>   nodes: A, B, C
#>   edges: Ao-oB, Bo-oC
